title: The Outer Automorphism Exact Sequence 1 → Inn(G) → Aut(G) → Out(G) → 1

problemStatement.plain: Every group G has an automorphism group Aut(G). The inner automorphisms are the maps conj_g : x ↦ g·x·g⁻¹; the parent entry showed g ↦ conj_g has kernel Z(G), so Inn(G) ≅ G/Z(G). This follow-up formalizes that Inn(G) is a normal subgroup of Aut(G), so the quotient Out(G) = Aut(G)/Inn(G) is a group, and assembles the short exact sequence 1 → Inn(G) → Aut(G) → Out(G) → 1.
whyMatters: Out(G) is a fundamental invariant measuring symmetries of G not realized by conjugation; it governs group extensions and the theory of complete groups (Z(G)=1 and Out(G)=1 give Aut(G) ≅ G).
The sequence promotes the parent's G/Z(G) ≅ Inn(G) from an isolated isomorphism into the first term of the canonical exact sequence organizing the automorphism tower.
Computations of Out(G) for simple groups (e.g. the exceptional Out(S₆)) are classification-level data that all rest on this exact sequence.

open: Define Inn(G) as (MulAut.conj (G := G)).range : Subgroup (MulAut G) as a first-class object.
Prove Inn(G) is normal in Aut(G) via the identity φ ∘ conj_g ∘ φ⁻¹ = conj_(φ g).
Define Out(G) := MulAut G ⧸ (MulAut.conj).range and prove exactness: ker π = Inn(G), π surjective, ι injective.
knownResults.goal: Define Inn(G) = (MulAut.conj).range, prove Subgroup.Normal, define Out G := MulAut G ⧸ Inn G, and assemble the short exact sequence 1 → Inn(G) → Aut(G) → Out(G) → 1 with exactness at each term, reusing the parent's G/Z(G) ≅ Inn(G) to describe the first term.
